intro: Washington D.C., a city with a rich historical background and the epicenter of American politics, is home to some of the most iconic landmarks in the country. From the grandeur of the White House to the legislative prowess of the Capitol and the solemnity of the Supreme Court, the city is a living, breathing testament to the nation's democratic ideals. But beyond the corridors of power, Washington D.C. offers a vibrant cultural landscape, with world-class museums such as the Smithsonian Institution, where you can explore a treasure trove of galleries and exhibitions for free. The city's neighborhoods, from the upscale charm of Georgetown to the trendy H Street Corridor, offer a delightful mix of dining, shopping, and entertainment to suit every taste.

explore.label: Nature
paragraphs: Washington DC is a vibrant city that also offers a wealth of green spaces and natural beauty, making it a perfect destination for outdoor enthusiasts. Rock Creek Park, one of the largest urban parks in the United States, spans over 1,700 acres and provides a sanctuary for hiking, biking, and picnicking. The park’s trails are lined with lush forests and historic landmarks, offering a tranquil escape from the bustling city. For those seeking a more serene experience, the U.S. National Arboretum features 446 acres of gardens and woodlands, showcasing a diverse collection of plants and trees, including the famous azalea collection and the National Bonsai & Penjing Museum.

The Potomac River is another natural gem in DC, offering a range of water activities and scenic views. Guests can rent kayaks or canoes to explore the river’s calm waters, or take a leisurely stroll along the Georgetown Waterfront Park, which features a boardwalk, picnic areas, and stunning views of the river. The Anacostia River Trail, accessible from various points in the city, provides a peaceful path for walking, running, or cycling, making it easy to enjoy the natural beauty of Washington DC while staying at one of Marriott Bonvoy’s conveniently located hotels.

explore.label: Culture
paragraphs: The culture in Washington D.C. is a vibrant mix of the city’s historical significance and its diverse community. Staying at a Marriott Bonvoy hotel in Washington D.C. places you at the epicenter of this dynamic cultural hub, where every corner tells a story. Explore the many iconic monuments and museums that celebrate the nation’s heritage, or delve into the city’s rich African American history at the National Museum of African American History and Culture. After a day of discovery, unwind in the comfort of your hotel, knowing that the convenience and luxury of Marriott Bonvoy are just steps away from the heart of the city’s cultural landmarks.

To further immerse yourself in the city’s arts and culture, be sure to visit the Smithsonian American Art Museum and the National Portrait Gallery, where you can view works that span centuries and reflect the city’s artistic spirit. Washington D.C. is also a food lover’s paradise, with a thriving culinary scene that offers a mix of international flavors and local favorites. From Michelin-starred restaurants to bustling food markets like Union Market, you can taste the flavors that define this city.

explore.label: Climate
paragraphs: Washington D.C. is a city of four seasons, each with its own unique charm. Summers (June to August) are warm and humid, with temperatures often reaching the 80s and 90s. Afternoon thunderstorms and occasional heat waves are common, so it’s best to plan indoor activities or take advantage of the city’s many shaded parks and air-conditioned museums. The city’s proximity to the Potomac River can offer a refreshing breeze, and many Marriott Bonvoy hotels provide amenities like pools and air-conditioned rooms to keep you comfortable.

Winter in Washington D.C. is cool and crisp, with temperatures hovering between the 30s and 50s Fahrenheit. Snowfall is moderate, creating a postcard-worthy setting around the city’s famed monuments. Fall and Spring, from September to November and March to May, respectively, are the prime time to explore the city’s outdoor spaces. With temperatures in the 60s and 70s, it’s the perfect weather to visit the National Mall and its cherry blossoms or to take a stroll through the parks and gardens to witness the vibrant fall foliage. Whether it’s warm or cold outside, Marriott Bonvoy hotels in Washington D.C. are ready to welcome you with the amenities you need for a comfortable and memorable stay.

explore.label: Transport
paragraphs: Washington D.C. offers plenty of convenience when it comes to transportation, and you have a multitude of options for getting around when you stay at one of Marriott Bonvoy’s many hotels. The city is served by two major airports, Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport and Dulles International Airport, both of which offer a variety of ground transportation services, including taxis, ride-sharing apps like Uber and Lyft, and the city’s efficient Metro rail system. Many of our Washington D.C. hotels also offer complimentary shuttle services to and from the airports, making your arrival and departure as seamless as possible. If you’re arriving by train, Union Station is the city’s central hub and offers direct connections to the Metro, allowing you to easily reach any part of the city.

Once in Washington D.C., the Metro is an excellent choice for getting around, with five lines covering major neighborhoods and attractions. Buses and the DASH system offer additional routes and are particularly useful for exploring more specific areas. Taxis and ride-sharing services are widely available and provide a convenient way to travel directly to your desired destination. For those who prefer to drive, car rental services are available at various locations, including the airports. Washington D.C. is also bike-friendly, with Capital Bikeshare stations throughout the city, and many of the city’s historic sites and popular attractions are within walking distance from central Marriott Bonvoy hotels.

explore.label: Kids
paragraphs: Washington D.C. is a treasure trove of educational and fun activities for the whole family. Start your adventure at the National Air and Space Museum, where children can explore interactive exhibits, climb aboard a real airplane, and even see a moon rock. Another must-visit is the National Zoo, home to a wide array of animals, including giant pandas, Asian elephants, and rare species from around the globe. The zoo’s Kids’ Farm and interactive feeding sessions are sure to keep the little ones entertained and engaged.

intro: Seattle, a city that needs no introduction, is a must-visit destination that seamlessly blends natural beauty with urban sophistication. From the iconic Space Needle to the bustling Pike Place Market, the city offers a wealth of attractions that cater to every interest. Marriott Bonvoy’s hotels in Seattle provide the ideal starting point for your exploration, ensuring you are always close to the best the city has to offer. Whether you’re here for business or leisure, the comfort and convenience of our properties, along with their proximity to major landmarks and transportation hubs, make your stay both memorable and stress-free.

explore.label: Nature
paragraphs: Seattle is a haven for nature enthusiasts, with its wealth of verdant parks and awe-inspiring natural vistas just moments away. The iconic Discovery Park, sprawling across 534 acres, beckons with its extensive network of trails, panoramic views of the Puget Sound, and the chance to spot local wildlife. If you prefer the curated beauty of botanical gardens, the Washington Park Arboretum awaits, offering 230 acres of diverse plant collections for a serene stroll or a peaceful picnic.

If you’re seeking water-based activities, Seattle’s proximity to the Puget Sound and Lake Washington offers endless possibilities. Kayaking and paddleboarding are popular in the city, with rentals available at several locations, including Golden Gardens Park and Alki Beach. For a more tranquil experience, the Hiram M. Chittenden Locks in Ballard provide a unique look at the marine life and the engineering feat that connects the freshwater lakes to the saltwater sound. Whether you’re a seasoned hiker or a casual nature walker, Seattle’s natural beauty is certain to captivate and inspire.

explore.label: Culture
paragraphs: The culture in Seattle is a vibrant tapestry woven from a blend of innovation, arts, and a deep appreciation for nature. Staying at one of our hotels in Seattle places you at the epicenter of this dynamic city, where you can explore the historic Pike Place Market, a bustling hub of local artisans, farmers, and musicians. The city's creative spirit is further showcased at the Chihuly Garden and Glass, where the stunning glass installations of Dale Chihuly inspire awe and admiration. After a day of cultural exploration, unwind in the comfort of your Marriott Bonvoy accommodations, featuring modern amenities and cozy retreats that capture the essence of Seattle's modern yet welcoming vibe.

Seattle's music and performing arts scene is as legendary as it is diverse. From the iconic Museum of Pop Culture, which celebrates the city's contributions to music and pop culture, to the intimate venues of Capitol Hill, where up-and-coming artists share the stage with local legends, there's always a melody in the air. The city also boasts a thriving theater community, with venues like the Seattle Repertory Theatre and the Intiman Theatre offering a range of productions that reflect the city's progressive and inclusive culture. Whether you're a music enthusiast or a theater lover, Seattle's cultural offerings are sure to leave a lasting impression. Explore more of Seattle's arts and culture.

explore.label: Climate
paragraphs: Seattle is known for its temperate oceanic climate, which ensures mild temperatures throughout the year, making it a delightful destination any season. Summers, from June to September, are generally warm and dry, with average highs in the 70s and lows in the 50s, providing the perfect weather for exploring the city’s vibrant outdoor markets, parks, and waterfront areas. Rainfall is minimal during these months, but occasional afternoon showers can occur, so it’s wise to carry a light jacket or umbrella. Marriott Bonvoy hotels in the city offer comfortable amenities, including outdoor terraces and rooftop bars, where you can enjoy the pleasant summer evenings.

Winter in Seattle, from December to February, is cool and wet, with temperatures ranging from the mid-30s to low 50s. Snow is rare, but the city is often lush and green thanks to frequent rain, which averages around 20 inches during the season. Spring and fall, from March to May and September to November, are mild, often foggy, and range from the 50s to 70s. These seasons are ideal for exploring the city’s gardens, with spring flowers in full bloom and fall foliage in its prime. Whether you’re visiting for the rainy charm of winter or the mild, refreshing weather of spring and fall, Seattle’s climate adds a unique flavor to your stay.

explore.label: Transport
paragraphs: For those flying into Seattle, the city is easily accessible through Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, one of the largest and busiest airports on the West Coast. The airport provides a variety of transportation options, including the SeaTac Airport Station, which is connected to the city by the Sound Transit Light Rail, offering a swift and efficient journey to downtown and other key areas. Taxis and ride-sharing services such as Uber and Lyft are also readily available, ensuring a smooth transition from the airport to any of the city’s Marriott Bonvoy hotels. Those arriving by train can take advantage of Amtrak’s King Street Station, which offers direct connections to major hotels and attractions.

Once you're in Seattle, the city is yours to explore. The public transportation system is extensive and easy to use. The Sound Transit Light Rail and the Seattle Streetcar are great options for getting around quickly and seeing the sights. The King County Metro bus system is a good way to get to areas outside the city center, and it connects many neighborhoods and popular destinations. Taxis and ride-sharing services are also available. If you prefer to drive, you can rent a car at the airport or in the city. Seattle’s downtown area is compact and easy to walk around, and there are many attractions within walking distance of each other. You can also rent a bike from one of the city’s bike-sharing programs.

explore.label: Kids
paragraphs: Seattle is a haven for families seeking adventure and shared enjoyment. Begin your journey at the Pacific Science Center, where children can immerse themselves in interactive exhibits, marvel at exciting science demonstrations, and enjoy a film at the IMAX theater. A visit to the Seattle Aquarium promises a day of joy and discovery, with opportunities to observe lively otters, stately sea lions, and vibrant fish. The interactive touch pools and engaging educational programs ensure that learning about the wonders of the sea is both enjoyable and lasting.

When it’s time to let the kids run and play, head to Discovery Park, one of the largest and most beautiful urban parks in the city. With miles of trails, a beach, and a playground, it’s the perfect spot for a family picnic and outdoor exploration. For a unique experience, visit the Museum of Pop Culture, where kids can explore the world of music, movies, and pop culture through interactive exhibits and workshops. Whether you’re exploring the city’s cultural gems or enjoying its natural beauty, Seattle has something to captivate and delight every young adventurer.

intro: Denver, a city that effortlessly marries the beauty of nature with a cosmopolitan flair, is yours to explore. Known as the Mile High City, Denver serves as a gateway to the majestic Rocky Mountains, beckoning outdoor enthusiasts to hike, bike, or ski. The city's cultural tapestry is rich, with a myriad of museums such as the Denver Art Museum and the Denver Museum of Nature & Science, and the vibrant arts district of RiNo. Our collection of Marriott Bonvoy’s hotels in Denver is strategically located near key attractions, offering amenities that promise a comfortable and memorable stay.

explore.label: Nature
paragraphs: Denver is your gateway to the great outdoors, offering a variety of natural wonders that cater to every kind of adventurer. Just a short drive from the city, the Rocky Mountains provide endless opportunities for hiking, mountain biking, and rock climbing. Red Rocks Park, known for its iconic amphitheater, also features scenic trails and breathtaking views, making it a must-visit for nature lovers. For those seeking a more leisurely experience, the Denver Botanic Gardens offer a tranquil setting with over 15,000 plant species, including themed gardens like the Japanese Garden and the Mordecai Children’s Garden, perfect for a peaceful stroll or a family outing.

Denver's City Park is a vast urban oasis that's home to the Denver Zoo and the Denver Museum of Nature & Science. Here, you can immerse yourself in both the natural world and the rich cultural heritage of the region. For a more up close encounter with the mountains, the foothills surrounding Denver are peppered with state parks and nature reserves. Outdoor attractions like Bear Creek Lake Park and Chatfield State Park offer lakes for water activities, trails for exploration, and even camping areas. Whether you're a seasoned outdoor enthusiast or simply savor the beauty of nature, Denver's varied landscapes and meticulously maintained parks ensure there's always a fresh adventure to embark upon.

explore.label: Culture
paragraphs: Denver's culture is a rich tapestry, reflecting the city's history, diverse arts, and love for the outdoors. Marriott Bonvoy's collection of hotels in Denver provides the perfect starting point for exploring the city's cultural riches. From the impressive American Indian art to modern masterpieces and the iconic Frederic C. Hamilton Building at the Denver Art Museum, to the interactive exhibits at the History Colorado Center, there's something to captivate every visitor. After a day of discovery, return to the comfort of your Marriott Bonvoy hotel, where modern amenities and a warm welcome await.

Denver’s creative pulse beats through more than just its museums. The city’s street art is a living, breathing entity, and its many art and culture festivals are a testament to the city’s commitment to the arts. In the RiNo Art District, you’ll find yourself surrounded by murals, sculptures, and street art that transform the neighborhood into an urban gallery. And throughout the year, events like Denver Arts Week and the Five Points Jazz Festival offer live performances, workshops, and community celebrations. Denver’s cultural scene is sure to inspire and delight seasoned art lovers and casual exploreres alike.

explore.label: Climate
paragraphs: Denver is known for its high-altitude, semi-arid climate, which means you can expect plenty of sunshine and mild weather throughout the year. In the summer months, from June to August, you can look forward to warm, dry days with average highs in the 80s and 90s. This is the perfect time to get out and explore the city's outdoor attractions, from the nearby Rocky Mountains to the many parks and festivals. Keep in mind that while the days are toasty, the evenings can cool down quite a bit, so it's wise to have a light jacket on hand. Our Marriott Bonvoy hotels in Denver offer the ideal home base for your summer getaway, complete with outdoor pools and air-conditioned rooms for your comfort.

Denver winters are cold but not too snowy, with daytime temperatures typically in the 30s and 40s and nighttime temperatures in the 20s. The city gets about 55 inches of snow each year, making it a great destination for winter sports. Spring and fall are mild with temperatures in the 50s to 70s. These seasons are great for hiking, biking and enjoying the city's many cultural events. Whether you visit in the summer or winter, you'll find that Denver's climate is comfortable and enjoyable, and Marriott Bonvoy hotels offer thoughtful amenities to make your stay even better.

explore.label: Transport
paragraphs: Denver International Airport is one of the largest and busiest airports in the nation, with a wide variety of transportation options to get you to your hotel. The A Line commuter rail offers a direct and scenic route to downtown Denver. Other options include taxis, ride-sharing services like Uber and Lyft, and rental car facilities. Many Marriott Bonvoy hotels offer complimentary shuttle services to and from the airport, making your trip even easier.

Once you're in Denver, getting around is a breeze. The Regional Transportation District (RTD) operates a vast system of buses and light rail lines to take you to all the major attractions, neighborhoods, and business districts. If you're looking for a more flexible way to travel, ride-sharing services and bike-sharing programs like B-cycle are also available. And if you'd rather drive, you can easily rent a car from one of the many car rental companies in the city. No matter where you're headed, Denver's diverse transportation options make it easy to get there.

explore.label: Kids
paragraphs: Denver is a city that caters to families, offering a plethora of kid-friendly activities to keep everyone engaged. A visit to the Denver Zoo is a must, with over 4,000 animals to discover and interactive exhibits like the Primate Panorama and the Toyota Elephant Passage. The Children’s Museum of Denver is another great choice for a hands-on experience, where kids can learn and play in areas like the Construction Zone and Water Ways, designed to inspire curiosity and creativity.

For those with a love of the great outdoors, Denver is the gateway to the Rocky Mountains, where you can hike, bike, or picnic in parks like Red Rocks or City Park. If you prefer to stay closer to the city center, the Denver Botanic Gardens offer a peaceful and educational experience, with beautiful floral displays and engaging programs for young visitors. Refuel at one of the many family-friendly restaurants in the city, where you’ll find something for everyone on the menu.

Music City offers a variety of unforgettable experiences and music venues, from the iconic Grand Ole Opry to the historic Ryman Auditorium. Beyond the music, Nashville is a thriving cultural hub with a rich history, stunning art galleries, and a burgeoning culinary scene that showcases the best of Southern cuisine. Whether you're a music enthusiast, a history buff, or a food lover, Marriott Bonvoy's hotels in Nashville provide the perfect base for your exploration.

explore.label: Nature
paragraphs: Nashville, a city famous for its music, also has a lot to offer in terms of natural beauty. Centennial Park is a large urban park in the city that is perfect for picnics, jogging, or just enjoying a sunny day. The park is home to a full-scale replica of the Parthenon, which is a must-see for anyone visiting Nashville. If you're looking for a more immersive nature experience, the Nashville Zoo at Grassmere is a great place to visit. The zoo is located on 200 acres and has a wide variety of animals and scenic walking trails.

Just a quick drive from the city, the trails of Radnor Lake State Natural Area are waiting for you to enjoy a peaceful walk through the woods and along the lake. This protected area is a great place to see wildlife and to get away from the city. If you're up for more of a challenge, Percy Warner Park has more rugged trails and great views. It's a great place to go for a morning hike or an afternoon bike ride. Whether you prefer a quiet walk by the lake or a more challenging hike through the hills, Nashville’s natural beauty offers something for everyone.

explore.label: Culture
paragraphs: Known as the "Music City," the sound of live music is ever-present in Nashville, from the iconic honky-tonks of Broadway to the grand concert halls of the arts district. Marriott Bonvoy’s collection of hotels in Nashville is thoughtfully designed to immerse you in the city, with amenities that seamlessly complement the local scene, such as rooftop bars and music-inspired decor. Step outside and explore the iconic Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum to trace the origins of American country music, or take a leisurely stroll through the hallowed halls of the Ryman Auditorium, where the echoes of past performances still linger. At the end of the day, find solace in the comfort of your Marriott Bonvoy accommodations, where Nashville’s spirit is met with a touch of luxury and ease.

When you stay at one of our Nashville hotels, you can expect to be surrounded by the city's rich culture. Nashville is known for its music, but it's also a city of art and culinary delights. The art scene is booming, with the Frist Art Museum and the Tennessee State Museum showcasing a variety of works from local and international artists. And the food scene is just as vibrant. In the 12 South neighborhood, you'll find upscale boutiques and quirky eateries, and you can't leave town without trying the classic hot chicken. Whether you're sipping a craft cocktail at a trendy bar or taking a peaceful stroll through Centennial Park, Nashville's mix of old and new ensures there's always something exciting to discover.

explore.label: Climate

The summer months, from June to August, bring warm days and balmy nights, with average high temperatures in the 90s Fahrenheit. Afternoon thunderstorms are a common occurrence, offering a dramatic interlude to the day's activities. After a day of exploring, our Marriott Bonvoy hotels provide the perfect retreat with air conditioning and pool amenities to keep you cool and refreshed.

Snowfall is minimal, usually just a few inches a season, so you can enjoy the city without the harsh conditions of other destinations. Spring and fall are the best times to visit, with temperatures in the 60s to 70s and beautiful blooms in the spring and colorful foliage in the fall. These seasons are perfect for outdoor activities, and a stay at a Marriott Bonvoy hotel will put you in the best position to experience everything the city has to offer.

No matter how you choose to get around, you'll find that Nashville is set up so you can easily explore and enjoy everything the city has to offer.

intro: Memphis, the heart and soul of the American South, is a city that resonates with the music of legendary artists. As the home of the blues and the birthplace of rock 'n' roll, Memphis invites you to step back in time and explore its rich musical history, from the iconic Beale Street to the cherished estate of Graceland. Marriott Bonvoy’s collection of hotels in Memphis are strategically located to provide you with easy access to the city’s cultural and historical landmarks, ensuring a seamless and enriching experience as you discover the Mississippi River, indulge in Southern cuisine, and immerse yourself in the city’s heritage.

explore.label: Nature
paragraphs: Memphis is a city that seamlessly blends urban charm with lush natural landscapes, making it a perfect destination for those seeking a breath of fresh air. The Mississippi River, a majestic waterway that runs through the heart of the city, offers endless opportunities for outdoor enthusiasts. Take a leisurely stroll along the River Walk, where you can enjoy scenic views and perhaps spot some local wildlife. For a more adventurous day, hop on a kayak or paddleboard and explore the river's quieter coves, or join a guided river tour to learn about the area's rich history and ecology.

Shelby Farms Park is a 4,500-acre urban park that offers a variety of outdoor activities and opportunities to connect with nature. The park features more than 40 miles of trails for walking, running and biking, as well as fishing in its lakes and ponds. The Greenline is a 10.65-mile-long urban trail that connects Midtown Memphis to Shelby Farms Park, making it perfect for a scenic bike ride or jog. The park also features a Dog Park and Playground, making it a great place for families to spend time together. The Memphis Botanic Garden is a 96-acre garden that features 28 specialty gardens, including a Japanese Garden, Rose Garden, and Butterfly Garden.

explore.label: Culture
paragraphs: Memphis is a city where the soulful notes of blues and the pulsating beats of rock 'n' roll have shaped a unique cultural landscape. Beale Street, the city’s iconic thoroughfare, is a living testament to this musical heritage, with its historic clubs and bars where legends like B.B. King and Elvis Presley once performed. The Memphis Rock 'n' Soul Museum offers an immersive journey through the city’s musical evolution, from the early days of the blues to the birth of soul and rock 'n' roll. Beyond music, the city’s cultural tapestry is rich with art and history, making it a must-visit for anyone seeking a deep connection to the roots of American culture.

For those who appreciate art and history, Memphis is a treasure trove. The National Civil Rights Museum, located at the former Lorraine Motel, offers a moving and comprehensive look at the civil rights movement, including the balcony where Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated. The Memphis Brooks Museum of Art houses an impressive collection of American and European art, with a focus on contemporary and rotating exhibits. The city’s artistic spirit is also reflected in its many murals and public art installations, adding a vibrant and dynamic element to the urban landscape and celebrating the creativity and tenacity of its residents.

explore.label: Climate
paragraphs: Memphis is a city of contrasts, with a humid subtropical climate that brings warm summers and cool winters, making it a great year-round destination. Summer in Memphis is hot and humid, with temperatures often reaching the low to mid-90s. Afternoon thunderstorms are common, providing a welcome break from the heat. Whether you're exploring the city's rich musical heritage or taking a leisurely stroll along the Mississippi River, you'll find that our air-conditioned hotels with pools are the perfect place to cool off and relax after a day of sightseeing.

Memphis winters are generally mild, with daytime temperatures in the 50s and nighttime temperatures in the 30s. Snowfall is rare and light, so you can easily visit indoor attractions like museums and galleries. Fall and spring are particularly pleasant, with temperatures ranging from the 60s to the 80s. Fall is the perfect time to see the leaves change, and in the spring, the city is filled with blooming flowers. These seasons are ideal for outdoor activities, and staying at a Marriott Bonvoy hotel in downtown or the Midtown area will put you within walking distance of many of the city's top attractions.

explore.label: Transport
paragraphs: When you arrive in Memphis, you’ll find an array of transportation options to get you started on your trip. Many visitors fly into Memphis International Airport, where you can easily catch a taxi or use ride-sharing services like Uber and Lyft to get to your hotel. Some Marriott Bonvoy hotels in the area also offer complimentary airport shuttle services for added convenience. If you’re traveling by train, the Amtrak City of New Orleans route stops in Memphis. Greyhound bus services and an extensive network of highways also provide additional access to the city.

Once you're in Memphis, getting around is a breeze. The Memphis Area Transit Authority (MATA) operates an efficient network of buses and trolleys. Taxis and ride-sharing services are also widely available. Many visitors choose to rent a car, and there are plenty of rental options, including at the airport and at Marriott Bonvoy hotels. Downtown Memphis is very walkable, so you can easily explore the area on foot. But for attractions like Graceland, a short drive or ride-sharing trip is your best bet.

explore.label: Kids
paragraphs: Memphis is a city that never fails to entertain and educate its younger visitors. The Memphis Zoo is a must-see, home to over 500 species and exciting exhibits like the Teton Trek and the Zambezi River Hippo Camp. For more interactive fun, the Children’s Museum of Memphis is the place to be, with its life-sized grocery store and a genuine FedEx airplane for the little ones to explore.

For the history and music enthusiasts in your family, a visit to Graceland is a must. Step into the world of Elvis Presley and learn about his legendary life and career. The Pink Palace Museum is another great place to visit. It offers a variety of exhibits, including dinosaurs, a planetarium, and the Court of the Wild Beasts, which features live animals. If you want to enjoy the great outdoors, head to Shelby Farms Park. With activities like paddle boating, horseback riding, and plenty of open space to run and play, it’s the perfect place to spend a sunny day. Refuel with some delicious, kid-friendly barbecue at Central BBQ or Corky’s Ribs & BBQ.

intro: Welcome to Austin, the vibrant capital of the South, where the laid-back charm of the Southwest meets a thriving tech industry and a bustling arts scene. Known as the “Live Music Capital of the World,” Austin offers an endless array of music venues, from the iconic Sixth Street to the more relaxed Zilker Park, where you can enjoy free concerts and festivals. Marriott Bonvoy’s hotels in Austin provide a perfect home base, ensuring you’re always close to the city’s top attractions, too, including the Texas State Capitol, the LBJ Presidential Library, and the unique Barton Springs Pool.

explore.label: Nature
paragraphs: Austin is a haven for nature enthusiasts, with a perfect balance of city life and stunning landscapes. Zilker Park, a vast 351-acre escape, beckons you to its hiking trails, picnic spots, and the renowned Barton Springs Pool, a natural swimming pool with a constant, cool temperature, fed by an underground spring. The Lady Bird Lake Hike and Bike Trail is a favorite, meandering 10 miles around the lake, offering stunning vistas for runners, cyclists, and those out for a leisurely stroll. The Barton Creek Greenbelt is a peaceful retreat, with its trails through a scenic canyon, inviting you to explore and enjoy the city's natural splendor.

If you are looking to engage with the tranquility of nature, the Austin Nature and Science Center is a great place to start. The center offers interactive exhibits and outdoor spaces that are both educational and inspiring. The Hamilton Pool Preserve is another hidden gem just a short drive from the city. The preserve boasts a 50-foot waterfall that plunges into a natural pool, surrounded by limestone cliffs and lush vegetation. Whether you are an experienced hiker, a casual walker, or a nature lover, Austin’s outdoor attractions offer something for everyone and are sure to leave you with lasting memories.

explore.label: Culture
paragraphs: The culture in Austin is a vibrant tapestry of creativity, music, and culinary innovation that sets it apart from any other city. Staying at a Marriott Bonvoy hotel in Austin means being just steps away from the thriving live music scene, where you can catch impromptu street performances or head to iconic venues like the Continental Club and Stubb’s BBQ. The city’s eclectic neighborhoods, each with its own unique charm, offer endless opportunities to explore local art galleries, craft breweries, and farmers markets. Austin’s dedication to preserving its heritage is evident in the historic buildings and landmarks, such as the Texas Capitol and the Driskill Hotel, which blend seamlessly with modern amenities and a laid-back, welcoming atmosphere.

For the food enthusiast, Austin is a haven of flavors, from the renowned food trucks that line the streets to the upscale dining options downtown. The cuisine is a reflection of the city's varied influences, with Tex-Mex, barbecue, and farm-to-table dining taking center stage. Austin's commitment to sustainability and local sourcing is evident in its numerous farmers markets and community-supported agriculture programs. Whether you're enjoying a plate of brisket at Franklin Barbecue or dining at a Michelin-starred restaurant, the culinary landscape in Austin is as dynamic and inventive as the city itself.

explore.label: Climate
paragraphs: Austin is a year-round destination with a humid subtropical climate, characterized by long, hot summers and mild winters. From June to August, temperatures often reach the 90s and can even hit triple digits, making it the perfect time to explore the city's indoor attractions and enjoy the comfort of air conditioning. Thunderstorms and occasional afternoon showers keep the city's green spaces lush and provide a welcome break from the heat. Many Marriott Bonvoy hotels in Austin offer outdoor pools and indoor spas, providing the perfect way to relax and refresh during your stay.

Winter in Austin is generally mild, with daytime temperatures in the 50s to 60s and nighttime temperatures in the 40s. While snow is rare, you may experience a few chilly mornings. Spring and fall are the most pleasant seasons, with daytime temperatures in the 70s to 80s. These seasons are perfect for outdoor activities, as the city's parks and gardens are filled with colorful blooms in spring and the foliage in fall provides a beautiful backdrop. Whether you're in town for a festival, to catch some live music, or to explore the great outdoors, Marriott Bonvoy hotels provide the perfect home base to enjoy Austin's climate and all the city has to offer.

explore.label: Transport
paragraphs: Travelers to Austin are in luck, as the city is easily accessible via the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, with a range of transportation options at your fingertips. From taxis to ride-sharing services like Uber and Lyft, to airport shuttles provided by many Marriott Bonvoy hotels, getting to your accommodation is a breeze. For those arriving by land, Amtrak’s train services and Greyhound bus lines also serve the city, and its well-connected highways make for a smooth drive.

Once in Austin, the city is yours to explore. The Capital Metro provides an extensive network of bus routes and a light rail system to connect you to all the key areas and attractions. Taxis and ride-sharing services are also widely available, offering a flexible and efficient way to get around. And if you prefer to drive, there are plenty of car rental agencies located both at the airport and throughout the city. Austin’s downtown area is particularly walkable, and many of its top attractions are within easy reach from Marriott Bonvoy’s central hotels. Whether you prefer to drive, take public transit, or simply stroll, Austin ensures that you have a seamless experience navigating its dynamic neighborhoods and iconic landmarks.

explore.label: Kids
paragraphs: Austin is a treasure trove for the young and young at heart, offering an abundance of activities that are sure to ignite the spark of imagination and creativity. Kick off your family's next escapade at the Thinkery, a haven for interactive learning and play, where children can immerse themselves in everything from building robots to unraveling the mysteries of the natural world. The Austin Zoo is equally compelling, providing up-close encounters with a diverse array of wildlife and educational programs that inspire a love for conservation. For a one-of-a-kind outdoor adventure, Zilker Metropolitan Park beckons, with the opportunity to splash in the iconic Barton Springs Pool, meander through scenic trails, or savor a picnic amidst breathtaking vistas.

The Bullock Texas State History Museum is also a hit with families. Kids can learn about the state’s history through interactive exhibits and an enormous IMAX theater. The city’s music scene is legendary, and you can take the family to a kid-friendly concert at the Austin City Limits Live at the Moody Theater or the Long Center for the Performing Arts. After a day of fun, treat yourself to some ice cream at Amy’s Ice Creams or a casual meal at Frank’s Drive-In. With so many kid-friendly options, Austin makes sure every moment of your family vacation is unforgettable.

explore.label: Nature

Just a short drive from the city center, the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area beckons with its peaceful waters and scenic trails. Whether you're a fan of kayaking, fishing, or simply unwinding with a riverside picnic, this expansive area has something for every outdoor enthusiast. For a more immersive experience, the Atlanta Botanical Garden awaits, with its meticulously curated gardens, enchanting waterfalls, and a vast conservatory housing plants from all corners of the globe.

Nature enthusiasts will appreciate the verdant forests and undulating landscapes of Stone Mountain Park, with its colossal granite outcrop providing a dramatic setting for outdoor activities such as hiking, biking, and rock climbing. The park's trail system, which includes the challenging Summit Sky Hike, offers panoramic vistas of the city skyline and the surrounding woodlands. Closer to the city center, Piedmont Park is a haven of greenery, ideal for a jog, a game of frisbee, or a leisurely day in the sun. Atlanta's diverse natural attractions ensure that every visitor can find a tranquil escape from urban life.

paragraphs: The city of Atlanta is a rich tapestry of historical significance, cutting-edge innovation, and the warm embrace of Southern hospitality. Selecting one of our Atlanta hotels places you at the heart of a city that has been a key player in the civil rights movement and is a current hotspot for culinary and artistic discovery. It's a place where old-world charm and modern sophistication coexist, from the historic district to the lively River Street. Each corner of Savannah is an invitation to step back in time while enjoying contemporary comforts. With Marriott Bonvoy’s collection of hotels in Savannah as your base, you're perfectly positioned to explore the city’s top attractions, from the iconic Forsyth Park to the vibrant art scene.

explore.label: Nature
paragraphs: In Savannah, nature and history are in perfect harmony. The city offers a variety of outdoor experiences for all types of adventurers. Forsyth Park, a 30-acre park in the heart of the city, is a popular green space with a large fountain, tree-lined walkways, and the Fragrant Garden, a garden designed to delight the senses. Tybee Island Beach is a short drive from the city and is a great place to relax on the sand, swim in the Atlantic, and enjoy the coastal breeze. The Savannah Botanical Gardens is a 33-acre site with landscaped gardens and natural areas that are perfect for a leisurely stroll or a picnic.

For those who enjoy the great outdoors, the Bonaventure Cemetery offers a hauntingly beautiful experience with its Spanish moss-draped live oak trees and peaceful ponds. It's the perfect place to take a quiet stroll, reflect, or capture some stunning photographs. Nature lovers will also enjoy a visit to the Oatland Island Wildlife Center, where they can observe alligators, birds, and deer in their natural habitat, surrounded by a variety of ecosystems. Whether you're exploring the city's parks or venturing out to the coast, our Marriott Bonvoy Savannah hotels put you in the perfect position to experience the best of the city's natural beauty.

explore.label: Culture
paragraphs: Savannah’s historic district is a living museum of Southern charm and heritage, where antebellum architecture, cobblestone streets, and lush squares create a backdrop for the city’s rich cultural tapestry. Staying at one of our hotels in Savannah places you in the heart of this vibrant scene, making it easy to explore the Telfair Museums, the oldest public art museum in the South, or the impressive Owens-Thomas House & Slave Quarters, which offers a deep dive into the city’s past. The city’s annual Savannah Music Festival and the colorful First Friday art walk further highlight its commitment to the arts, ensuring there’s always something new to discover.

And then there’s the food. Savannah’s culinary scene is the stuff of legend, with traditional Southern cuisine meeting modern innovation. From the upscale restaurants in the historic district to the family-owned eateries in the neighborhoods, the city’s food tells a story of its cultural influences. Be sure to try local favorites like shrimp and grits, crab cakes, and sweet tea at some of the city’s most popular spots. After a meal, take a leisurely walk through Forsyth Park, where the fountain and the atmosphere reflect the city’s spirit.

explore.label: Climate
paragraphs: Savannah is known for its warm subtropical climate, making it a great place to visit any time of the year. The summer months of June through August are warm and humid with temperatures often reaching into the 90s. Afternoon thunderstorms are common and help to cool things down. Staying at a Marriott Bonvoy hotel in the city center will give you access to our indoor and outdoor pools and air-conditioned rooms, so you can stay cool and comfortable.

Winters in Savannah are generally mild, with daytime temperatures averaging in the 60s, and cooler evenings in the 40s and 50s. The city sees minimal rainfall and almost no snow, making it a perfect escape for those seeking a break from colder climates. Spring and fall, from March to May and September to November, are particularly pleasant, with temperatures ranging from the 70s to the 80s. These seasons offer ideal weather for exploring the city’s historic district, enjoying outdoor festivals, and strolling through the beautiful squares and parks. Marriott Bonvoy hotels provide the perfect base for all your seasonal adventures, ensuring a comfortable and memorable stay.

explore.label: Transport
paragraphs: For those visiting Savannah, there are a number of transportation options to make your trip as smooth and enjoyable as possible. The city is easily accessible by air, with the Savannah/Hilton Head International Airport serving as the primary gateway for those flying in. Once you arrive at the airport, you can get to your accommodations by taxi, ride-sharing services such as Uber and Lyft, or by taking advantage of your hotel’s complimentary shuttle service, if available. For those who prefer to travel by land, Savannah is also well-connected by Amtrak and Greyhound, both of which offer convenient rail and bus services. Additionally, Savannah is a popular stop for those on a road trip, as it is easily accessible by major highways.

Once you're in Savannah, getting around is a breeze. The Savannah Transportation System offers an extensive network of buses to take you all around the city. Taxis and ride-sharing services are also available for more direct or flexible transportation. For a more immersive experience, consider renting a bike or taking a guided tour. The historic district is especially charming on foot. Many of Marriott Bonvoy’s hotels in Savannah are centrally located, so you can easily walk to nearby attractions, dining, and shopping. Whether you choose to drive, walk, or use public transportation, Savannah offers the freedom to explore at your own pace.

explore.label: Kids
paragraphs: Savannah is a city that bursts with family-friendly fun, from its enchanting historic district to its lush green spaces. Start your adventure at the Savannah Children's Museum, where hands-on exhibits and the popular Bubbleology show will captivate young minds. For a dose of nature and play, head to Forsyth Park, which features a large playground, a splash pad, and plenty of open space for picnics and games. The park's iconic fountain is a must-see and a perfect spot for family photos.

The Georgia Aquarium’s sister facility, the Savannah Children's Museum Aquatic Adventures, is a must-visit for animal lovers. Here, kids can learn about marine life and even touch a stingray. For a unique experience, take a family-friendly pirate cruise on the Savannah River. These exciting voyages offer treasure hunts, storytelling, and interactive fun that will keep the whole family entertained. After a day of exploring, enjoy some delicious, kid-friendly dining options at local favorites like Mrs. Wilkes' Dining Room or The Collins Quarter.
